key_insight: Three-dimensional URANS global stability analysis shows that screeching jets remain governed by coupled Kelvin–Helmholtz and shock-cell feedback loops, even in strongly under-expanded turbulent regimes.
engineering_relevance: The results help explain and predict jet noise mechanisms in under-expanded nozzles, supporting improved aeroacoustic design and control strategies.
method: Solve compressible URANS with dNami for turbulent screeching jet fixed points
Linearize the discrete system via Tapenade and compute global modes with a time-stepping stability solver
Use Helmholtz decomposition and energy budgeting to separate vortical/irrotational contributions
evidence_signal: Fixed-point flows and extracted modes were validated against experimental and numerical data, including comparison with experimental POD showing correct wavenumber content and spatial organization.
watch_item: The approach depends on accurate URANS fixed points and linearization around them, so performance may be sensitive to modeling fidelity in highly nonlinear flow regimes.
paper_title: Three-dimensional global stability analysis of turbulent screeching jets
